desc: Asymmetric predator/prey simulation - wolves hunt deer with different action sets and win conditions.

desc: Large-field battle simulator - 500 personality-driven actors, unit-level personalities, simulated ballistics, cover and melee. Same seed, same battle.

name: Pack Hunt 3D

desc: Pack Hunt in 3D - the same wolves and deer with an energy and gait model, on an orbitable field. A second, independent implementation in Godot 4 / GDScript, exported to WebAssembly.

name: Pack Hunt Brains
short: Describe the herd and the pack in plain English; Claude compiles both and runs them.
desc: Tell the deer herd and the wolf pack what to do, in plain English. Claude compiles each side into a small behaviour language and the simulation runs them against each other - the language picks actions, the energy model decides what they cost.

name: War Sim (Godot)
short: War Sim rebuilt in Godot 4 and WebAssembly - the same battle, a second engine.
desc: War Sim in Godot 4 / GDScript, exported to WebAssembly - a second, independent implementation of the same 500-actor battle, deterministic by seed.

name: Rock Bots
short: 5v5 robots throwing rocks and punching - a personality-driven ragdoll brawl in Godot 3D.
desc: Five-a-side robot brawl in Godot 4 / WebAssembly. Robots throw reusable rocks (three sizes; damage from the rock's mass and speed relative to the target, friendly fire on) and punch (wind-up, can miss, can be dodged); six hitboxes per robot, a hit does more the more of them it catches; every knockdown is a ragdoll. They only dodge and aim at what they can see, never throw through a mate, and guard their friends. Pure spectator AI sim: pick a preset (Brawler, Slinger, Coward, Tactician, Guardian, Balanced) or seven sliders per team (aggression, caution, rock love, teamwork, patience, survival, protect), watch at 1-8x with pause, or batch-run matches for stats. No clock - last team standing; the winners dance, then squat on and relieve themselves over the fallen before the results panel asks whether to go again.

name: Melee Bots
short: 5v5 robot brawl with rocks, bats, knives, swords and spears - get floored, drop your weapon.
desc: The armed cousin of Rock Bots (Godot 4 / WebAssembly). The arena is strewn with rocks (thrown, three sizes), bats, knives, swords and spears (knives and spears can be thrown too), one thing per robot and editable in setup. Every knockdown makes you drop what you hold, a landed weapon blow always floors its target, and being hit cancels the swing you were winding up - so between two robots swinging at each other, he who connects first keeps his weapon. Fists, feet and stomps as in Rock Bots; robots see only what is in front of them, never throw through a mate, and guard their friends. Presets or seven sliders per team, pause, 1-8x, batch stats; the winners dance, squat on and relieve themselves over the fallen.

name: Dodgeball Bots
short: 6v6 dodgeball where each player's five build properties add up to 1 - spend them well.
desc: Six-a-side elimination dodgeball as a spectator AI sim (Godot 4 / WebAssembly), on NDL / USA Dodgeball rules: the opening rush for six balls on the centre line, live balls, catches that put the thrower out and bring a teammate back, blocking with a ball in hand, the ten-second throw clock and the possession rule. Each player has a personality (six sliders: aggression, caution, catching, teamwork, patience, bully) and a build of five properties - speed, arm, aim, hands, dodge - that always add up to 1; push one up and the rest give way. The exchange rate between properties was set by simulation: a team of specialists in any one property beats an even team about half the time (tools/calibration_report.md in the repo). Presets or sliders per team, pause, 1-8x, batch stats, and a headless sim with an aim-test harness.

name: The Outdoor Office
short: An office made of rocks and logs. Present from a boulder, out-influence your nemesis.
desc: A turn-based influence game in a Godot 4 world drawn to look like a graphic novel. The office is made of natural elements: slab-stone desks on stump legs, slate monitors, a felled-log break room, a stream instead of a water cooler, and a flat-topped boulder you present from. You and a work nemesis alternate turns. Four actions each: take a prop from a desk, which also makes the nearest neutrals curious; work the stream, which converts curious neutrals into followers but does nothing for cold ones; or rally in the break room. Then walk to the rock and give a three-slide talk to whoever turns up. Everyone in the crowd wants one of data, story, gadget or snacks, and a slide lands in proportion to how much of the room was hoping for that. Between slides a heckler interrupts and you either eat a small boo or clap back. Boo pressure net of applause peels followers off you and turns them into haters, so a talk can lose you the round even when it is loud. Seven archetypes - neutral, follower, wage slave, influencer, lover, hater, bully - each a pump or a drain on the shared pool of neutrals, which is what the two of you are actually fighting over. The nemesis turn plays out in the world at 3x so you can watch it happen. Three rounds, then a head-to-head card of claps, boos and people gained. The look is three layers: a banded toon shader with a cool purple shadow tint instead of a darker one, inverted-hull ink outlines expanded radially so box corners stay watertight, and a Forward+ depth and normal edge pass for interior creases. Animation is quantised to 12 fps, which is most of what makes the figures read as drawn rather than simulated. Keyboard and mouse on desktop, thumbstick and a TALK button on a phone.

name: The Outdoor Office: Party Battle
short: Lead a party through the office, loot the desks, then give the final talk.
desc: A tactics battle on a 31 by 19 office floor, drawn on a legal pad. You pick a job, spend four points on Charm, Guile, Hustle and Grit, and bring up to four colleagues; your nemesis brings as many. Every colleague is a unit with morale and a job ability on a cooldown: Rally, Prototype, Jam, Counsel, Rumour, Pitch, Injunction, Fetch. For twelve turns each unit moves and does one thing - argues with an adjacent enemy, pickpockets a card, takes a card from a desk, raids a supply closet, pitches a neutral into your crowd, hires a contractor or retains a consultant in the Lobby, or rigs the projector at the Rock. A unit at zero morale drops its cards as loot and sulks in the car park; put the whole enemy party there at once and the match is yours. Otherwise both leaders give a final talk with every card their party still holds, scored by quality and by how many in the room want each taste. The rules engine and its planner are plain JavaScript with no DOM; a headless harness plays the planner against itself (level over 100 matches) and against random play (never wins). The earlier board-game version is still at /board.html.

name: Dance-Off Bots
short: 5v5 street dance-off: dance in step to score, or break off and floor the other crew.
desc: A five-a-side street dance-off as a spectator AI sim (Godot 4 / WebAssembly) to a generated 120 BPM beat. Every two bars the showiest dancer still standing calls the next move from eleven in three tiers; the crew scores sync for dancing it together on the beat and flair for how well and how boldly they dance it, with hats and canes adding polish. Anyone who stops to punch, barge, fetch a prop or fling a bin lid scores nothing until the next phrase - except a dance-strike, a kick or swing that lands on the beat of a real move, which scores and floors a rival. Three judges weigh sync and flair differently and hold up their cards; the winners cheer and the losers sit down and cry. Each crew has a personality (aggression, showmanship, discipline, grudge, caution, teamwork) and a build of five properties - rhythm, flair, balance, strength, arm - that always add up to 1. Presets or sliders per crew, pause, 1-8x, sound toggle, batch stats and a headless sim with a calibration tool.

name: Legion Bots
short: TABS-style ragdoll battles: spend 500 gold on Brawlers, Slingers and Shields, place them, and watch them fight.
desc: A TABS-style army battle on the Rock Bots model (Godot 4 / WebAssembly). Spend 500 gold a side on three unit classes - Brawler, Slinger and Shield - tap or drag to place them on your half, give each squad a type (brawn, speed, grit, reflex, aim, always adding to 1) and a personality, and press Fight. There are no orders: how a squad holds, charges or hangs back comes from its personality. Up to 20 a side, three preset armies, five saved-army slots in the browser, and a results panel with gold spent and gold left standing. Unit costs are placeholders until they are calibrated by simulation.
